title: V.E.T.O.R — Ruptura: building a cinematic adventure with Flow video scenes, AI dialogue and a locally voiced robot
author: Sufficient-Cause2216
selftext:
Hi! I'm Jonie, a solo developer from Brazil working on V.E.T.O.R — Ruptura, a Windows adventure that mixes side-view exploration, RPG progression and conversations with NPCs. I'm sharing the project here because generative AI is a substantial part of its development, and I want to explain how it fits into the playable experience.



I generated video scenes with Google Flow and integrated them into the game. The challenge has been connecting those scenes to player movement, timing, interface elements and story state. A video can look convincing on its own, but the transitions and controls still have to work when someone is actually playing. Some of the voice work also uses synthesized and cloned voices derived from generated material.



The companion robot, VETOR, can respond to the player through AI dialogue. For its current voice, I am testing Kokoro locally: a blend of 65% pm\_alex and 35% pm\_santa, shifted up one semitone. The game tries Kokoro first, Edge TTS second and a Sopro voice fallback last if the earlier options fail. The local voice approach is intended to run on the player's computer instead of requiring a shared speech server for every player.



The game is still in development and there is no public playable build yet. The project page has screenshots and gameplay trailers: [https://jonie-magno-rangel.itch.io/vetor](https://jonie-magno-rangel.itch.io/vetor)



For people working with generated video in games, how do you keep transitions between exploration and cinematic scenes consistent without making the controls feel interrupted? That has been one of the most useful problems to work through on this project.
